name: Eurostat migr_resocc
provides: First permits for remunerated activity by permit category x citizenship x member state x year
notes: The dependent variable. Suppressed cells arrive as null and are dropped rather than zero-filled.

name: Eurostat migr_resfirst
provides: All-reason first permits (employment/family/education/other)
notes: Context and denominators.

name: Eurostat migr_pop1ctz
provides: Resident population by citizenship (context only; no longer the diaspora variable)
notes: DROPPED as the diaspora source. It is a reporting series, and seven destinations publish no third-country citizenship detail: France reported African citizenships in 2018 and never again, Denmark stopped after 2022, and Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Malta and Poland never have. Spain reports ten of fifty-four. Zero-filling that made the panel assert no Moroccans live in France. Replaced by UN DESA.

name: Eurostat jvs_a_rate_r2
provides: Job vacancy rate total and by NACE sector
notes: No s_adj dimension on this dataset.

name: Eurostat nama_10_a10 / nama_10_a10_e
provides: Compensation of employees and employment by sector - sector pay
notes: Compensation in EUR million divided by employment in thousands.

name: Eurostat une_rt_a
provides: Unemployment rate

name: Eurostat demo_pjanind
provides: Old-age dependency ratio
notes: Structural demand proxy.

name: World Bank World Development Indicators
provides: Income, unemployment, education, demography, urbanisation, internet, remittances
notes: Latest non-null observation per country within the window.

name: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators
provides: Corruption, government effectiveness, political stability, rule of law, regulatory quality, voice
notes: Codes are GOV_WGI_*.EST; a country/all query returns empty ISO3 codes so the country list is named explicitly and batched.

name: CEPII GeoDist
provides: Distance, contiguity, shared official and ethnic language, colonial relationship, common coloniser
notes: Ships as .xls inside the zip. Uses 2011-vintage codes (ZAR/ROM) and predates South Sudan; aliased and haversine-filled respectively.

name: OpenFlights
provides: Direct airline route counts (fallback only)
notes: DEMOTED to a fallback. A 2014 community snapshot of SCHEDULED routes only; it returned zero direct routes on 1,331 of 1,458 corridors, including Egypt-Poland. Now used only where Eurostat publishes no airport-pair data, which is Czechia alone.

name: Wikidata
provides: Diplomatic missions by operating state and host state
notes: Embassy coverage is good and cross-checks against known posting counts (France 49 African embassies). Consulate coverage is thinner and is fetched as an optional supplement.

name: CIA World Factbook
provides: Religious composition and official languages
notes: Free text parsed to shares. Reported granularity is uneven so the religion vector is deliberately coarse. Raw source string retained on every row.

name: ISO 3166 with UN M49 codes
provides: ISO2/ISO3/M49, UN region and intermediate region
notes: The join spine.

name: Curated agreements register
provides: Bilateral labour agreements, EU Talent and Mobility Partnerships, CPLP mobility, Decreto Flussi preferential quotas
notes: NEEDS EXPERT REVIEW BEFORE CITATION. Every row carries a source URL and its own confidence flag.

name: ICMPD/ECDPM master pathway files
provides: Policy attributes, sector tags and origin eligibility for 354 EU legal pathways
notes: Referenced by the concept note but not publicly available. The largest fidelity gap; ease-of-unlocking is built from public substitutes instead.

name: DG HOME Schengen visa statistics
provides: Short-stay visa applications and refusals by Schengen state and country of application; also the authoritative list of where visa applications can be lodged
notes: Short-stay (Schengen C) not work permits - a friction proxy. Ireland is outside Schengen and Cyprus reports separately; both fall back to Wikidata.

name: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform
provides: Median daily welfare in 2021 PPP; one half of the blended income measure
notes: Reports consumption for most African countries and income for most European ones - the welfare_type column is carried through so the mismatch stays visible. Uses PIP's fill_gaps lined-up estimates, which project each country's latest survey to a common reference year via national-accounts growth; complete coverage, but old-survey origins are projections. SCORING uses the average of this median and WDI PPP GDP per capita: the median understates worker earnings (consumption basis, informal economy), GDP pc overstates them (a mean including the capital share), and the blend splits the difference. Both figures are reported on every corridor card.

name: WHO health workforce support and safeguards list
provides: Countries where active international recruitment of health personnel is discouraged
notes: 55 countries, 40 of them among our origins. Flag only - never enters a score. The 2026 update was still unpublished as of Aug 2026; the May 2026 Global Code amendment extended the Code to care workers but did not reissue the list.

name: world.geo.json country outlines
provides: Country polygons for the map
notes: Five small island states (Cabo Verde, Comoros, Mauritius, Sao Tome, Seychelles) are absent from the source and are drawn as capital markers instead.

name: ICMPD/ECDPM/MPF Labour Pathways mapping
provides: Roster of legal labour migration pathways across the EU-27; title, description, link
vintage: fieldwork to Feb 2024; records modified late 2024
notes: API returns 295 pathways (MPF note says 294; the concept note's 354 is unverified anywhere public). Structured attributes (country, sector, quota, salary, language, labour market test) are Pods fields not exposed to REST, and /pods/v1 is 401. The country-to-pathway join is NOT recoverable - ID-order grouping was tested both ways against slug fingerprints and fails. No country assigned. Policy signals parsed from description text are derived, not ICMPD fields.

name: UNHCR Refugee Data Finder
provides: Bilateral refugee and asylum-seeker stocks
notes: Needs coo_all/coa_all flags; plain coo=/coa= filters return an empty item list rather than an error. 414 Africa-EU pairs carry stock.

name: UCDP battle-related deaths via World Bank
provides: Conflict intensity at origin
notes: The concept note names UCDP/PRIO directly; that API now requires an access token, so the World Bank's republication of the same UCDP series is used. Origin coverage 52%.

name: Hofstede six-dimension cultural scores
provides: Cultural distance (Kogut-Singh)
notes: 14 African countries surveyed individually; Hofstede's own Africa East / Africa West / Arab clusters used where they plausibly apply; Middle Africa and most of Southern Africa left unavailable.

name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics
provides: Tertiary graduates by ISCED field of study (health & welfare, ICT, engineering, agriculture, services, business, STEM) and share of 15-24s in vocational education
notes: Field-of-study data for 44 of 54 origins. Shares of all graduates, not headcounts; combine with population for scale. The ISCED fields map onto the tool's occupation families, which is what lets the sector overlay use origin supply.

name: WHO Global Health Observatory
provides: Health workforce density: nurses and midwives, and doctors, per 10,000 population
notes: Complete for all 81 countries. Origin median 11.7 per 10k against 82.6 in destinations. The one occupation with a direct headcount on both sides.

name: Curated destination requirements register
provides: EU Blue Card and general permit salary thresholds, language requirements, qualification recognition regimes and key route requirements for all 27 destinations
notes: NEEDS EXPERT REVIEW. Thresholds move annually by statute. Explicit numeric thresholds are on file for a minority of states; the rest carry a described basis. Every row has a source URL and its own confidence flag.

name: Curated outsourced visa centre register
provides: VFS Global, TLScontact and BLS International centres processing applications for each destination in each origin country
notes: 129 corridors. NEEDS VERIFICATION - operator networks change frequently. Scored below an in-country mission but well above having to cross a border.

name: Eurostat migr_resfirst (education reason)
provides: Bilateral first residence permits issued for study
notes: Already downloaded for context and previously unused. 127,622/yr Africa-EU student permits against 118,010 work permits - students are the larger flow.

name: Derived Africa-orientation penalty
provides: Share and breadth of a destination's mapped pathways that are reserved for non-African nationalities
notes: Derived, not an ICMPD field. Detects Balkans, Eastern Partnership, Asian and Anglosphere nationality restrictions in pathway text, weights by how many occupation types the route covers, and cuts the destination's usable-pathway score by up to 40%. 16 of 27 destinations affected; Slovenia takes the maximum.

name: EURES / European Labour Authority shortage occupations
provides: Occupations more than half of reporting countries identify as in shortage, with country counts and severity
notes: Table 2 of the report, parsed and asserted at 24 rows. EU-wide, NOT per country: the per-country answers for all 436 four-digit ISCO occupations exist only inside a PowerBI embed with no documented query interface, which is too brittle to depend on. Absence from the table is not evidence of no shortage - the threshold is 'more than half of reporting countries', so concentrated shortages such as ICT do not appear.

name: Curated permit processing deadlines
provides: Statutory decision deadlines, the 45-day Talent Partnership track, and national statutory fast-track schemes
access: hand-assembled from EU directives and national authorities
notes: Built from law rather than from observed practice, because published per-country actuals come only from immigration-consultancy blogs that disagree with each other. Recast Single Permit Directive (EU) 2024/1233 Art 5 sets 90 days and a 45-day track for EU Talent Partnership applicants; Blue Card Directive (EU) 2021/1883 Art 11 also 90. Denmark and Ireland are outside both on Protocols 22 and 21 and run national regimes. Fast-track schemes recorded for Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark and Ireland; absence means NOT RECORDED, not that none exists.

name: Derived diaspora momentum
provides: Compound annual growth of the bilateral migrant stock, 2020-2024
notes: NOT net migration, which is a country total across all partners and says nothing about a corridor. Now derived from UN DESA 2020 and 2024 rather than Eurostat. UN DESA counts the foreign-born where a country has that data, so naturalisation does not erase people from it - a better construct for diaspora than citizenship. Measurable on 690 Africa-EU corridors.

name: UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024
provides: Bilateral migrant stock by origin and destination, 1990-2024
notes: The diaspora variable, replacing Eurostat. UN DESA estimates the full origin-by-destination matrix rather than passing through what states choose to publish, so every destination is covered: 9.27m Africa-EU migrants against Eurostat's 3.89m, the difference overwhelmingly France. Counts foreign-born where available, else foreign citizenship; the data_type column carries which. Pairs absent from the table are genuine near-zeros, not suppressed values - every listed pair carries a number. Fetched for all world origins, not just African ones, because the gravity model is estimated on the global panel.

name: Eurostat avia_par_<cc> airport-pair passengers
provides: Passengers carried between each EU airport and each partner airport worldwide, including non-scheduled traffic
access: REST API, one dataset per reporting country
notes: Air connectivity, replacing OpenFlights. Counts people rather than route entries, and covers charter traffic, which is much of the Europe-Africa network. The airport-pair code carries the partner country in its third field (PL_EPWA_TZ_HTZA is Warsaw-Zanzibar), which is what allows a country-level rollup. Best single year across 2019-2024 rather than the latest, because charters are intermittent - Warsaw-Zanzibar reports traffic in 2021 and no other year. Czechia does not disseminate avia_par_cz. Small charters below the reporting threshold do not appear at all, so absence is not proof of no service.

name: Curated language family classification
provides: Family and subfamily for every official language in the panel, plus documented high-intelligibility overrides
notes: Lets language scoring recognise relatedness instead of only exact overlap: a Lusophone origin now scores above a Swahili-speaking one when looking at Spain. Tiered (same language 1.0, same subfamily 0.60, same family 0.15) because that is all the classification supports. Same-family is only a token - Indo-European spans English to Greek to Polish. Six pairs where the tier badly misstates real intelligibility carry an explicit override with its basis recorded, including Afrikaans-Dutch above the West Germanic default and Maltese-Arabic below the Semitic one.

name: IMF World Economic Outlook (DataMapper)
provides: PPP GDP per capita where WDI has no series - Eritrea and South Sudan
notes: Fallback only: fills gdp_pc_ppp solely where WDI is silent, and every filled corridor carries the source and year on its card. Eritrea's series ends in 2019, when the country stopped engaging with the Fund - stale by construction. The API does not mark where outturns end and projections begin, so values are taken no later than two years back; South Sudan's next year showed a modelled +47% rebound no measurement produced. Unit mismatch acknowledged: WEO PPPPC is current international dollars against WDI's constant 2021.

name: Schengen Visa Code representation arrangements
provides: Which member state receives visa applications on behalf of another where the latter has no consulate
notes: KNOWN GAP, quantified 2026-09. Under Visa Code Art 8 a member state without a post is represented by another - in Cote d'Ivoire Belgium receives for Austria/Luxembourg/Netherlands/Sweden and France for Greece/Hungary/Malta/Latvia/Lithuania. The tool models neither this nor the small states' VFS arrangements, so f_consular reads 5-20 for 21 corridors that between them move 1,398 permits a year; Luxembourg and Malta account for 13 of them. Understates access for the ten destinations absent from vfs_centres.csv (BGR CYP EST HRV LTU LUX LVA ROU SVK SVN). Partial understatement, not total: representation covers short-stay type C, while long-stay work visas are generally reserved to the represented state's own posts, which is consistent with those corridors carrying real but modest flows.
